key_insight: Light can reversibly switch halide ions in 2D mixed-halide perovskites through strong light–lattice coupling, enabling defect-free photo-induced optical changes.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a route to self-resetting, light-programmable perovskite optoelectronic devices without relying on permanent ion migration or defect formation.
method: NEB calculations mapped the halide-exchange activation pathway.
Photo-force simulations quantified non-equilibrium work from illumination.
Lattice-dynamics and GW calculations linked soft phonons and bandgap renormalization to the observed optical response.
evidence_signal: The model reproduces experimental absorption spectra and predicts a light-induced redshift consistent with bandgap renormalization and partial halide swapping.
watch_item: The effect is partial and depends on illumination-driven non-equilibrium forces, so device stability and controllability under real operating conditions still need validation.
paper_title: Reversible photo-switching optical functionality in two-dimensional mixed-halide hybrid perovskites
